```markdown
# SEC filing-index ingestion — Roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md (§3 R1–R11 as outcome candidates); ranking and track confirmed by partner, 2026-11-10. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). | uv workspace with four member packages (root `pyproject.toml`). | Azure platform per the ADR, which is Proposed and not yet accepted (see Open questions).

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | A baseline filing-index catalog built from the archived quarterly indexes over a chosen range | A | 1 | Requests small: about one quarterly index plus listings per quarter, 4 quarters per year of range, at the 3 req/s target (§4.3, §4.8). Bytes and parse time per quarter: measured by Stage 1. |
| O2 | The catalog kept current from daily indexes, catching up after missed days | A | 2 | About one daily index per business day (~250 per year) plus listings; request cost not material. |
| O3 | Downloaded indexes turned into a validated, deduplicated filing-index table in Parquet with provenance | A | 3 | Measured by Stage 1. |
| O4 | The system running on Azure: ADF schedules, Container Apps Jobs runs the Python, ADLS holds files, Table Storage holds state, Azure Monitor holds logs | A | 4 | Azure spend cannot be estimated without running; measured by the Stage 7 smoke test (§7 step 4). |
| O5 | Backfill, daily ingestion and reconciliation sharing one downloader, parser and publisher, differing only in which sources they pick | A | 5 | Not material. |
| O6 | Stored raw index files reprocessed after a parser change, with no new download | A | 6 | Storage grows with every retained snapshot; size per snapshot measured by Stage 1. |
| O7 | Quarterly indexes re-read periodically, with later SEC changes recorded | A | 7 | One full re-read of every supported quarter per week (§4.8); request count equals O1's. |
| O8 | All SEC traffic going through one downloader and one request budget, however many workers run | A | 8 | Not material. |
| O9 | Readers getting each quarter through one versioned active pointer, never seeing half-written data | A | 9 | Not material. |
| O10 | No record leaving the catalog on a failure or an absence; closed-quarter removals only after hash-bound approval | A | 10 | Partner time per approval; frequency unknown until reconciliation runs on real data. |
| O11 | Schedules, retry limits and the request rate set from reviewed configuration | A | 11 | Not material. |

Tracks: A — SEC filing-index ingestion (known progression). One track: every outcome serves the same catalog, and none stands without the downloader and parser it shares.

Sequencing follows dependency, not the rank order. The core stage delivers O3 first, because every other outcome reads its parser and row contract. O4 (rank 4) moves to Stage 7: the stages before it run without Azure, so the code is proven on real data before the platform is built, and the ADR stays reversible until then. O8 (rank 8) and O9 (rank 9) come before backfill and daily discovery (ranks 1 and 2), because a wide collection run needs the shared request budget, and publication needs the pointer before it writes generations readers can see.

## Open questions

1. **Package layout.** §4.9 places all code in `packages/sec-edgar-ingest/`. The repository has four scaffold packages (`sec-edgar-client`, `sec-edgar-download`, `sec-edgar-index-ingest`, `sec-edgar-ingest`), and the root script `sec-edgar = "sec_edgar:main"` names a module that does not exist. Proposed default: Stage 1's brainstorming settles the layout and records it in its plan's Handoff.
2. **Acceptance.** The ADR and the spec are both Proposed (§7 step 1). Stages 1–6 do not depend on the Azure choice. Proposed default: acceptance is required before Stage 7 starts.
3. **Required values.** The SEC User-Agent identity is needed before Stage 1's real run. The backfill range and the daily handoff date (§4.8) are needed by Stage 8, and the range also sets which legacy formats Stage 5's fixtures must cover.

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Core — one real quarter and one real daily index, end to end
      Objective: Fetch one archived quarterly master index and one published daily master index from the SEC, and parse both into canonical rows written to Parquet.
      Outcomes: O3 (first slices of O1 and O2)
      Consumes: the package scaffolds; an SEC User-Agent (Open question 3)
      Produces: a fetch path that sends the User-Agent and stays at or below the §4.8 request target; a parser emitting the §4.5 `sec-index-v1` row contract for quarterly and daily formats; the package layout (Open question 1) in plan Handoff; specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O3 — one Parquet file per source holding `sec-index-v1` rows carrying `source_sha256`, with conflicting duplicates and malformed rows refused (§4.4, §4.6 Parse); the findings file records byte counts, row counts, elapsed time, peak memory and request count for the real run
      Leaves out: content-addressed raw store, source manifest and replay → Stage 2; shared lease, retry policy and §5 error outcomes → Stage 3; generations, manifest and active pointer → Stage 4; discovery from listings and legacy-format golden fixtures → Stage 5; reconciliation → Stage 6; Azure services → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Raw store, source manifest and replay
      Objective: Retain original bytes content-addressed, keep the source manifest, and reprocess stored inputs without SEC access.
      Outcomes: O6
      Consumes: Stage 1 fetch path and parser; plan <Stage 1>, Handoff
      Produces: content-addressed raw store; observations keyed by snapshot, parser and schema; the source manifest records (§4.5); the storage and state backing used before Stage 7, named in plan Handoff
      Exit: O6 — a parser-version change rebuilds observations from the raw store with SEC requests counted at zero, and an unchanged hash with unchanged versions is a no-op (§6 Replay)
      Leaves out: publication manifest and generations → Stage 4; Azure services → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: Shared collector and request budget
      Objective: Route every SEC request through one collector holding one request budget, with validated configuration.
      Outcomes: O8, O11
      Consumes: Stage 2 raw store and manifest
      Produces: one collector with a lease, retry policy, validation-before-acceptance and quarantine (§4.3); the §5 named outcomes for configuration, throttling, access blocks and lost ownership; typed configuration validated before I/O (§4.8)
      Exit: O8 — concurrent collectors in the §6 Access tests never overlap as request issuers, and retries count toward the budget; O11 — every §5 configuration refusal fires before any network request
      Leaves out: Azure-backed lease → Stage 7; schedules → Stage 7
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 4: Versioned quarter publication
      Objective: Publish each quarter as an immutable generation behind a conditional active pointer.
      Outcomes: O9
      Consumes: Stage 2 observations and backing store
      Produces: candidate generations with manifest and changes file; the conditional pointer update and repair (§4.5, §4.6 Publish); the publication-conflict outcome (§5)
      Exit: O9 — the §6 Publication crash-injection tests pass, and readers see only complete generations
      Leaves out: the withdrawal gate → Stage 6; Table Storage pointer → Stage 7
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 5: Backfill and daily discovery workflows
      Objective: Run backfill and daily ingestion as source selections over the shared discover, collect, transform and publish commands.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O5
      Consumes: Stages 3 and 4; the backfill range (Open question 3), which sets the legacy formats to cover
      Produces: the `discover`, `collect`, `transform` and `publish` commands with immutable worksets (§4.1, §4.2); open-quarter precedence (§4.4); golden fixtures across the chosen range (§4.6 Parse)
      Exit: O1 — a backfill over a fixture range reports complete, pending and failed units separately; O2 — the §6 Discovery and coverage cases pass, including an outage spanning quarters; O5 — backfill and daily runs call the same downloader, parser and publisher
      Leaves out: reconciliation → Stage 6; ADF orchestration → Stage 7; the real baseline campaign → Stage 8
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 6: Reconciliation and the withdrawal gate
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes and apply additions and updates, with closed-quarter withdrawals held behind hash-bound approval.
      Outcomes: O7, O10
      Consumes: Stage 5 commands and Stage 4 publication
      Produces: reconciliation as a source selection (§4.2); closed-quarter rules and approval records (§4.4); the withdrawal-pending outcome (§5)
      Exit: O7 — additions and field updates appear in the changes file with before and after values; O10 — the §6 Reconciliation cases pass: open-quarter absence keeps the key, closed-quarter removal waits for approval of the exact hash, and stale daily replay cannot resurrect a withdrawn key
      Leaves out: weekly schedule → Stage 7; the manual first run and gated-candidate resolution → Stage 8
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 7: Azure deployment, triggers disabled
      Objective: Deploy the shared worker on the ADR's Azure services in an isolated environment and run the integration and smoke tests.
      Outcomes: O4
      Consumes: Stages 1–6; ADR and spec accepted (Open question 2)
      Produces: versioned infrastructure, identities, jobs, pipelines and alerts (§4.1, §4.7, §4.9); Azure-backed lease, ADLS and Table Storage pointer; the release record of image digest and configuration revision
      Exit: O4 — the §6 Integration tests and Orchestration cases pass on isolated Azure resources, and the §7 steps 3–5 smoke test and raw replay record byte counts, row counts, elapsed time, peak memory, image digest, request rate and Azure spend
      Leaves out: trigger enablement, the baseline campaign and runbooks → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 8: Baseline campaign and scheduled operation
      Objective: Run the real backfill and daily catch-up, then enable the daily and weekly triggers after observed scheduled runs.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O7, O11 (operational)
      Consumes: Stage 7 deployment; the backfill range and daily handoff date (Open question 3)
      Produces: the published baseline; enabled triggers; runbooks and README (§8)
      Exit: O1 — every requested baseline unit is published or recorded as an approved gap; O2 — the daily trigger runs after an accepted catch-up; O7 — one manual reconciliation runs with gated candidates resolved, then the weekly trigger runs; O11 — the release record names the configuration revision in use (§7 Exit)
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note, or the plan header of a stage with no stage spec, carries:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, run SKILL.md §6 over the Outcomes list, O1–O11: one gap-rubric verdict per outcome, with evidence (implementing stage and plan, Deviation notes, deferred items). An unmet outcome exits as a new stage or as a deferral with a written reason.
```
